scenarios.behavior: Initial instruction revision is recorded; later revisions preserve predecessor, actor, reason, and time.
BLOCKED and READY tasks accept a revision using the current expected version and create a new version.
A stale expected version is rejected without overwriting the current instruction.
Unauthorized actors cannot revise, stop, or redispatch; task-control actions require a reason.
Revising a CLAIMED task revokes the old lease before the revised task is claimable again.
A RUNNING task receives a stop request, remains not-stopped until acknowledgement, and is not normally redispatched before acknowledgement.
Worker stop acknowledgement is idempotent; acknowledgement allows the task to return to the eligible claim state.
A revoked lease or stale revision cannot start, heartbeat, complete, submit results, or trigger dependent work.
Before acknowledgement, only ADMIN can force redispatch after confirming the duplicate-side-effect warning and supplying a reason; the action is audited.
OPERATOR cannot force redispatch without stop acknowledgement.
Completed task instruction and result remain unchanged, and correction work links to the completed task.
Task detail exposes current revision, active attempt revision, Worker, lease, stop acknowledgement, and revision history.
Empty, active, stopped, and completed task views and role-specific controls match task state and authorization.
Unrevised Worker claim/complete behavior remains compatible and migrations apply on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
